    What the photos show about the ground floor

    • The front is a wide flat face with five openings: window, tall lattice side panel, blue main door with a wooden toran above, tall lattice side panel, window.
    • Both front corners are cut at an angle. Each angled face is narrow, has one tall narrow window, and has a textured pilaster at each edge.
    • The round lattice window is on the ground floor, on the north-east side wall, just behind the front-right corner (as seen from the road).
    • The red tile eave and the roof parapet follow the angled outline, and the roof has a metal railing with pillars at the corners.

    Ground floor changes

    • New 5 ft patio all around the house, covered by the upper balcony. There are no pillars: the existing roof already projects about 3 ft past the walls, and the balcony slab is cantilevered out from the new floor, building on that projection.
    • Furnished: all three bedrooms (beds with the pillow side to the south-east, full-length wardrobes), the living room (TV wall, L-sofa, armchairs, coffee table), the lobby, the kitchen, both bathrooms and the two utility rooms. Choose Ground in the Inside tab to see it.
    • At the front this extends the porch by 5 ft, so the front steps and the retaining walls move 5 ft further out toward the courtyard.
    • The ground living room side door and the Bedroom 3 back door both open onto the patio.
    • Back extension: the two utility rooms now extend 2 ft further toward the back (north-west); the small bathroom between them stays the same size. The outside stair keeps its exact length and width and simply moves back 2 ft, with its top landing lengthened so it still reaches the main entrance.
    • Garden: the existing garden runs along the south-west side, about the length of the house, beyond the open terrace.

    Upper floor design

    • Same outline as the ground floor, so the walls and pilasters run straight up and the house reads as one building.
    • Windows sit directly above the ground openings and are larger, with clear glass in white frames.
    • Round window: on the ground floor the round lattice window and the narrow window swap places, so the round window now sits in the middle of the angled front-right corner (east) and the narrow window moves to the north-east side wall. A matching round window sits right above it upstairs, in the middle of the puja room's east wall, behind the mandir. The Today view still shows the house as it is now.
    • Wraparound balcony: 5 ft wide with a continuous railing on all sides, following the angled front. It breaks only at the back, along the 12 ft where the existing stair runs against the wall, because a balcony there would block headroom on the stair.
    • Directions: the front-right corner as seen from the road (the left corner when you stand at the main door looking out) points due east. So the front of the house faces south-east, the back north-west, the round-window side north-east and the terrace side south-west. The labels N, E, S, W and the side names are marked around the house in the 3D view and on the plans.
    • Arriving: the stair ends at a landing at the back. The main entrance is right there on the north-west (back) wall and opens straight into the living room. The gallery's glass door opens onto the front of the balcony.
    • Living room in the north corner. The kitchen is on the north-east side, with a glass door to the balcony, and the dining area is on the south-west side by the window. The mandir is in the east corner, on the angled wall that faces due east. All beds have the pillow side toward the south-east, or due south for Bedroom 3. Every wardrobe runs the full length of its wall, floor to ceiling. A glass door from the dining area on the north-east side opens onto the balcony.
    • Back bath: extended 2 ft toward the north-west, from about 8 × 5 ft to about 10 × 5 ft, over the extended ground utility rooms. All other rooms keep their sizes.
    • Front corners: Bedroom 3 and the puja room lose a small triangle and gain an angled wall. The bath and wet area moved to the south-west side, next to the gallery. The puja room has two windows: one toward the front and a narrow one on the north-east wall.
    • Plumbing: the back bath sits almost over the ground small bathroom. The second bath is on the south-west side, and the kitchen sink sits near the north-east wall so its drain can run straight down that outside wall.
    • Structure: with no pillars the whole 5 ft balcony is a cantilever, about 2 ft more than the existing 3 ft roof projection. It needs a properly reinforced slab tied back into the new floor, and the railing load at the edge must be allowed for. Many upper walls also do not sit over ground walls. A structural engineer should size the pillars, beams and foundations before any work starts.

    What is estimated

    • The angled corners are read from the photos: about 5 ft cut on each side, a 16 ft front face, and square back corners (the back is not in any photo).
    • Upper floor rooms come from the architect drawing, adjusted to the angled front. How it lines up with the ground floor is assumed.
    • Ground floor rooms come from your description, fitted to the same footprint. Labels show the sizes you gave.
    • Storey height is 10.5 ft. Stair shape, balcony and patio width (5 ft), the existing 3 ft roof projection, steps and courtyard are guesses. With the upper floor lifted, the stair is stretched to reach it.
